The SSH client (ssh.html) opens terminal sessions on SSH servers and transfers files over SFTP. It works like PuTTY with an integrated file panel. Connections go through the local relay (see the user guide, "Network functions and the relay").

Connecting

  1. New connection opens the connection dialog: name, host, port (22), user and the authentication: - Private key: paste the key (OpenSSH format -----BEGIN OPENSSH PRIVATE KEY----- or PEM) or load the key file; enter the passphrase if the key is protected. Ed25519, ECDSA and RSA keys are supported. - Password (also used for keyboard-interactive login).
  2. Enter the relay address and token once (they are stored with the connections).
  3. Connect opens a new tab; Save connection adds the connection to Saved connections (password and passphrase only if the box is ticked; a private key is always saved with the connection).

Host keys

When you connect to a server for the first time, the client shows the server's key fingerprint (SHA256:…). Compare it with the fingerprint the administrator gives you (ssh-keygen -lf /etc/ssh/ssh_host_ed25519_key.pub on the server):

  • Accept and save stores the fingerprint with the saved connection; later connections are accepted without a question.
  • Accept once connects without storing it.
  • Reject cancels the connection.

If the fingerprint of a saved connection changes, a warning is shown — someone could be intercepting the connection. Only accept the new key if you know why it changed (e.g. the server was reinstalled).

Terminal

Every connection opens a tab with a terminal (xterm-compatible, colours, mouse, resizing). The coloured dot shows the state: green connected, yellow connecting, red closed. Reconnect opens a closed session again; × closes a tab.

  • Select text to copy it with ⧉ (or the browser's copy shortcut); 📋 pastes the clipboard into the session.
  • Font size changes the size of all terminals.
  • ⏺ records the session from now on; a second click (⏹, showing the recorded size) stops and saves the log as a text file (without colour codes). ⤓ saves what the terminal currently holds (including the scrollback of up to 5000 lines).
  • On touch screens a key bar offers Esc, Tab, Ctrl (applies to the next key, e.g. Ctrl then C), the arrow keys and a few characters that are hard to type on phone keyboards.

Files (SFTP)

📁 Files opens the file panel of the session (it starts in the home directory):

  • Click a folder to open it, .. goes up; type a path and press Enter to jump there; ⟳ reloads.
  • Click a file (or ⬇) to download it.
  • Upload… uploads files into the current folder; you can also drop files onto the panel.
  • New folder, ✎ rename and × delete (folders must be empty).

Saved connections

Saved connections and the relay settings are kept in a connections file, a KeePass database (encrypted, recommended) or a JSON file (not encrypted). Use Save and Open… in the left panel. In KeePass, every connection is an entry in the group "Portable Web App Suite/ssh" with the private key and the host key fingerprint as additional fields (the key protected). A click on a saved connection connects; ✎ edits and × deletes it.

Known host keys: the left panel lists the host key fingerprints saved with connections; × forgets one, so the next connection asks again (e.g. after the server was reinstalled).

Creating a key pair

🔑 New key pair… creates a key for logging in without a password: Ed25519 (recommended), ECDSA P-256 or RSA 4096, with a comment and an optional passphrase that encrypts the private key. Afterwards the dialog shows the public key and its fingerprint: copy it into ~/.ssh/authorized_keys on the server (or save it as .pub), save the private key (id_ed25519, OpenSSH format, usable with OpenSSH and PuTTYgen), and Use in a new connection fills it into the connection dialog. Port forwarding is not possible in a browser (a page cannot listen on local ports).

In the file panel, ↗ (Open with…) opens a remote file in another application of the suite; saving there writes it back over SFTP.

Keyboard shortcuts

On a Mac, use Cmd instead of Ctrl. F1 (or ?) shows this list in the application.

Keys Function
F1 / ? show this list (outside of text fields)

On phones and tablets

☰ opens the saved connections. The file panel shares the screen with the terminal (below it). Use the key bar for keys missing on the on-screen keyboard.
